reason: Allowlist is a neutral alternative that avoids color-based metaphors and clarifies access control.
Blocklist avoids equating the color black with exclusion and mirrors current security terminology.
Master/slave metaphors reference enslavement; opt for precise role names such as primary/main and secondary/replica.
Slave terminology inherits oppressive metaphors; choose neutral descriptors like secondary or replica.
Sanity check implies ableism; confidence or quick check communicates the same intent without stigmatizing language.
Grandfathered stems from discriminatory policies; use neutral phrases like legacy or existing exemption to describe conditional access.
Guys assumes a masculine audience; folks or everyone are inclusive when addressing mixed groups.
Dummy can imply unintelligence; sample or placeholder describe test data without disparaging language.
Crazy carries ableist connotations; unexpected or erratic focus on the behavior instead of mental health.
Manpower and man-hours assume male labor; workforce or staff hours keep the phrasing gender-neutral.
Tribal knowledge can appropriate Indigenous cultures; institutional or team-specific knowledge conveys the concept respectfully.
